newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish business leaders call for more democracy.
newsitem.headline: Turkish business leaders call for more democracy.

text.p: Turkey's leading industrialists' association on Monday presented to parliament a report proposing a series of measures from electoral reform to Kurdish rights to reinforce the country's democracy.

A recent scandal linking public officials with underworld gangs was symptomatic of a growing threat to the democratic process, according to the report by the Turkish Industrialists and Businessmen's Association (TUSIAD).
Among its recommendations, the report said the threshold for a political party to be represented in parliament should be lowered to five percent of the national vote from ten percent.
The report detailed proposals to lift restrictions on the expression of Kurdish identity, such as allowing Kurdish-language broadcasts and names.
More than 12,000 people have died since 1984 in a conflict between soldiers and guerrillas fighting for Kurdish self-rule in southeast Turkey.

The report called for a shortening of periods in custody before charges are brought and closer observation of those held to prevent human rights abuses. International human rights monitors say detainees are often tortured in custody, something Turkish authorities deny.
Two government MPs face investigation over underworld links that surfaced in the wake of a car crash in which a police chief and a gangster died and a government MP was injured.
TUSIAD president Halis Komili said the crash should result in the identification of weaknesses and vulnerabilities in the system.
"The domination of daily life by...gangs is the price of having a system that proves unable to reform itself and retain public confidence," Komili told a news conference.
